bole.text: Stilt roots up to 25, widely spaced in a loose open cone, diagonal, branched near or below ground, terete, 1-2(-4) m long and to 9 cm thick, brown turning black, with spines to 2 cm (stem itself smooth). Cone height is not given: [1, 2] is the root length, and the roots are diagonal, so the cone is lower. Useful Tropical Plants: roots up to 3 m long. Crownshaft present and compact: 90-150 cm, greyish-green, densely white-tomentose when young (Mori et al.: cylindrical, glaucous green, to 1.5 m).

crown.text: About 7 spreading leaves (Henderson); 5-8 arching leaves forming a plumose crown (Mori et al. 1997). Mori calls it a canopy palm. 'open' density follows from the leaf count, not a stated value.

leaf.shape: pinnae 15-25 per side, asymmetrically cuneate (wedge-shaped) with a praemorse (jagged) tip; middle pinnae split to the base into segments; young plants hold the pinnae in one plane, older ones in many planes (plumose)

phenology.fruit: ovoid-cylindric, 2.5-3.5 x 1.5-2 cm, epicarp yellowish at maturity, splitting from the apex; seed 1.5-2.5 x 1-1.5 cm. Inflorescences to 90 cm, pendulous at anthesis.

bark.text: Stem grey and smooth with obscure nodes; 13-18 cm diam. at base, about 10 cm at apex.

palm.text: Henderson: stem 13-18 cm at base, about 10 cm at apex, nodes obscure (no ring spacing given); crownshaft 90-150 cm, greyish-green; petiole 15-40 cm; pinnae 15-25 per side, asymmetrically cuneate, praemorse, to 90 x 20 cm, the middle ones split into segments, in many planes in older plants; stilt roots up to 25, widely spaced in a loose open cone, diagonal, 1-2(-4) m long, to 9 cm thick, brown turning black. Mori et al. (src 1): 5-8 arching leaves.

habitat.range: Nicaragua south to Bolivia and east through Venezuela, the Guianas and Brazil

notes: Height: Wikipedia typically 15-20, to 25 m; Henderson to 20 m, usually less; UTP 8-25 m. Stem diameter: Wikipedia typically about 12, to 16 cm. Leaves: UTP about 7, 1.5-2 m long; leaf.length_cm is the rachis (Henderson 1.4-2.8 m), and the petiole adds 15-40 cm. Pinnae: Henderson to 90 x 20 cm, Mori to 100 x 30 cm; 40 cm is the proximal pinna. 'secondary/gaps' comes from UTP ('common in non-flooded fields and fallows'), and evergreen is assumed for a palm, not stated. Mori: on all soil and drainage types in French Guiana, never dense. Phenology: Wikipedia says flowering is mostly in the dry season (no region given); Mori: flowers and fruits year-round (French Guiana). No Madre de Dios or Osa months found. Fruit is yellow and edible (Wikipedia). White-lipped peccaries eat many seeds (Wikipedia); collared peccaries damage stilt-root tips (Spanish Wikipedia). The Napo camera-trap study covered Socratea spp. only. Palmweb blocked automated fetches.
